How the thesis works

Ten interactive diagrams covering what was built, what was measured, and where it falls short. Every number traces to a file in the study's repository, named in small print under each diagram.

1. Watch the model read a game

Drag the ply slider: the board, the two rating estimates, the attention weight, the per-move deviation and the running suspicion score all move with it.

Red ticks mark the plies where an engine move was planted. This game has 22 of them.
  • The two rating lines sit on top of each other because the network produces one shared estimate for the game. Diagram 8 measures that.
  • The whole-game pass lets every ply see the entire game, since the network reads the sequence in both directions. The running score rescores the game from ply 1 up to ply t, which is what a live viewer would have seen at that moment. The two are different computations and only agree at the last ply.
  • The label compares this score with ordinary held-out test games at the same time control. It is a percentile, not a verdict on the player.
  • The attention strip falls away toward the end of every game by construction, not because the model stops reading. Attention is masked so ply t may look only at plies 1 to t, and the weight drawn here is the average each ply receives across all the plies that can look at it, so a late ply has few of them.

data.text/markdown:
2. Anomaly detection, from zero

What a suspicion score is, what an AUC of 0.75 means, why checking more of a player's games helps, and how much cheating the detector can actually see.

2a. One game in, one number out

Every game gets a score between 0 and 1. Score thousands of games and the scores pile into two hills: honest games and games with engine moves. Where the hills overlap, the detector cannot tell them apart, so less overlap is a better detector. The AUC is exactly this: take one random engine game and one random honest game, and the AUC is how often the engine game gets the higher score.

data.text/html: <marimo-ui-element object-id='nWHF-0' random-id='a4f7df87-cb19-4d18-ae95-5eca972331d9'><marimo-slider data-initial-value='0.75' data-label='"\u003cspan class=\"markdown prose dark:prose-invert contents\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"paragraph\"\u003eDrag an AUC and watch the two hills pull apart\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e"' data-start='0.5' data-stop='0.99' data-step='0.01' data-steps='[]' data-debounce='false' data-disabled='false' data-orientation='"horizontal"' data-show-value='false' data-include-input='false' data-full-width='true'></marimo-slider></marimo-ui-element>

data.text/markdown:
2b. Checking more of a player's games, and part-time cheating

One game is noisy: a cheater can have an ordinary game and an honest player a brilliant one. Averaging a player's games cancels much of that luck, and cheating in only some games waters the average back down.

data.text/html:
Post hoc: a check on simulated players, run after the pre-registered player-level results were already reported.
  • A player's hand is built as a mix: a share f of their games come from a substituted cell and the rest are that player's own clean games, scored against the same clean players throughout. Withheld Maia bands, mean aggregation.
  • The number of cheating games in a hand is rounded up to at least one, so a player who cheats at all cheats at least once. At one game checked every share collapses to a fully cheated hand, and at five games the 10 and 25 percent shares both round to one game in five. That is why the curves dip from one game to five rather than rising.
  • The dashed line is a bell-curve picture, not a measurement. Tuned on one game and twenty. It undershoots beyond that, giving about 0.88 at both fifty and a hundred games where the measured curve reaches 0.893 and 0.915, because a single shared-noise term cannot reproduce how the real scores keep separating.
  • Players are simulated by pooling the detector's saved per-game scores: 500 cheating players per cell and 1000 clean players per band, seed 20260915, 200-replicate hierarchical bootstrap.

data.text/markdown: 2c. The measured curves

data.text/html:
Post hoc: The player-level aggregation of the sequence detector was not in the dated analysis plan. It was requested after that detector's per-game result was known, so it shows how an already strong score aggregates rather than confirming a prediction made in advance.
Every anomaly number here comes from synthetic games: Maia bots with planted engine moves. No real cheating accounts were available, so real-world accuracy is unknown.
  • Taking a player's worst game instead of their average was lower in every group beyond one game: 0.772 against 0.862 at 20 games on withheld bands.

data.text/markdown:
2d. How much cheating can it see?

The substitution rate is the share of the cheater's moves that were engine moves. The trained detector climbs as cheating gets heavier; the score that needed no training stays on the coin-flip line at every level.

data.text/html: <marimo-ui-element object-id='ZBYS-0' random-id='5a516ab8-6c9a-d4fc-dc21-ca9a575910c7'><marimo-dropdown data-initial-value='["Maia bands withheld from training"]' data-label='"\u003cspan class=\"markdown prose dark:prose-invert contents\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"paragraph\"\u003eEvaluation group\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e"' data-options='["Maia bands withheld from training","Bands seen in training"]' data-allow-select-none='false' data-searchable='false' data-full-width='false' data-disabled='false'></marimo-dropdown></marimo-ui-element>

At the 2 and 5 percent rates, the rates that describe occasional cheating, the trained detector is close to a coin flip. That is the weakest part of the result.
  • The dashed line is chance, and the bars are drawn from it rather than from zero, since an AUC below 0.5 is worse than guessing. Whiskers are 95 percent confidence intervals.
  • This is the summary-feature detector, which is not the sequence detector shown above it. On withheld bands at the 2 percent rate the sequence detector reaches 0.576 where this one reaches 0.539.
CCS Thesis - Integrated/chapters/chapter4.tex, supervised detector and computed score by substitution rate
Every value comes from synthetic games: Maia bots with planted engine moves. No real cheating accounts were available, so real-world accuracy is unknown.

A game has to clear every filter to reach the corpus
  1. Standard chess, so no variant games.
  2. Rated, which the archive records in the game's Event header.
  3. Both players carry a numeric rating in the headers.
  4. A real-time control written as base plus increment, which drops correspondence games and malformed entries.
  5. At least one move, and a clock annotation on every move up to the 100-ply cap, so the clock input is never guessed.

• Uniform reservoir sampling over each full monthly archive, so every eligible game of that month has the same chance of being kept no matter when in the month it was played. The animation is an illustration of the rule, not a replay of a real month.
  • The built store measures 11,494,612,992 bytes, verified byte-identical against its backup copy on 2026-08-27. The same corpus as loose pickle files is about 500 GB, which does not fit the cluster's 318 GB scratch disk. Chess position tensors are mostly zeros, which is why they compress so far.
  • A nested 90/10 then 80/20 game-level random split, matching the reference implementation. The split does not deduplicate by player.
  • A game that clears all five enters the month's reservoir. Only its first 100 plies are stored, which is truncation rather than exclusion.

data.text/markdown:
6. Did attention help? The paired bootstrap

Resample all 255,000 test games with replacement, take the mean difference, and repeat. Drag the slider to build the distribution.

data.text/html: Per game, the mean of the White and Black absolute errors. The paired delta is the full model minus the reproduced baseline. Each draw resamples all 255,000 games with replacement and takes the mean delta.

The confound control matters. Retraining the plain baseline at the higher learning rate alone accounts for 1.45 of the improvement; attention adds 1.63 on top of that, and both intervals clear zero.
  • Every arm is a single training run at training seed 0, so none of these points carries a seed-to-seed spread.
  • Recomputed here with the same games, the same 10,000 draws and the same seed, and it reproduces the recorded interval to four decimal places. The draws plotted are this recomputation.
  • The dashed red lines are the recorded 95 percent interval and the solid line is the recorded point difference. Zero is off the chart to the right, which is what makes the difference significant.

data.text/markdown:
7. Where the model is weaker

The study set itself a threshold: no subgroup may exceed twice the overall error. One does.

data.text/html:
Only the 2401+ bracket breaches the threshold, and narrowly: 350.62 / 171.92 = 2.04 for the full model and 354.27 / 175.00 = 2.02 for the reproduced baseline.
  • The improvement is not uniform. Attention lowers the error in three brackets, leaves one unchanged and raises it by 11.3 rating points in the lowest bracket.
  • A rating bracket counts each side of a game as its own sample under its own bracket, so the bracket counts sum to 510,000 while the time-control counts sum to 255,000 games.
  • The 50k-subset column is the baseline-reproduction sanity gate and is a pipeline reference point only, not comparable with the full-corpus arms.

data.text/markdown:
8. White and Black are one number

The network reports two rating estimates per game. Across all 255,000 test games they are almost the same number.

data.text/html:
• The two rows of the network's final layer have a cosine similarity of 0.9999, so that layer applies very nearly the same function twice. The released reference checkpoint behaves the same way, at 1.0000, so this belongs to the architecture and not to the attention work.
  • Replacing both estimates with their average leaves the overall test error unchanged, so the two numbers carry no separable per-side information.

9. The tuning sweep

Seventeen runs, each moving one setting around a fixed control. Six of them repeat the control exactly and give the sweep its own noise band.

data.text/html: <marimo-ui-element object-id='dlnW-0' random-id='24926a18-c271-dcbb-3ceb-5c80d185203b'><marimo-dropdown data-initial-value='["All factors"]' data-label='"\u003cspan class=\"markdown prose dark:prose-invert contents\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"paragraph\"\u003eFactor\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e"' data-options='["All factors","Attention dimension","Batch size","Dropout","Learning rate","Patience","Weight decay"]' data-allow-select-none='false' data-searchable='false' data-full-width='false' data-disabled='false'></marimo-dropdown></marimo-ui-element>

The shaded band is the six control cells, 222.31 to 223.75 around a mean of 223.19. A run inside it moved nothing.
  • Only the learning rate cleared that band by a clear margin, at 211.72. The adopted setting was re-run across five training seeds on the same subset for 213.23 plus or minus 0.78, and every seed landed above the single-run 211.72, so the five-seed mean is the confirmed figure.
  • Best-validation loss in rating points on the 170,000-game subset. These are not the full-corpus test MAE values reported elsewhere.
